title: Dominance-tree kernel selector + workload replayer for multi-objective autotune
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a small-footprint dominance-tree based selector and an offline workload replayer that together produce per-model, per-arch kernel-mix recommendations optimized for a multi-objective cost function (latency P95, tail latency, and GPU cycles). The system should accept historical request traces, microbenchmarks, and hardware profiles to synthesize Pareto front candidates and propose safe rollouts with fallback policies. The selector must be lightweight enough to run in the control-plane and produce per-shard suggested kernel profiles for runtime consumption.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Replayer ingests real request trace (JSON) and reproduces token-phase and seqlen distribution histograms within 3% of production metrics. 2) Dominance-tree selector outputs a ranked set of kernel-mix candidates and estimated cost/latency vectors. 3) End-to-end simulation predictions correlate with measured runtime P50/P95 within 10% on held-out workloads. 4) Proposal includes rollout plan (canary + fallback) and a PR for runtime integration hooks. 5) Minimal runtime overhead: selector config exchange <= 5KB and decision latency < 20ms in control-plane path.
design_notes: We avoid opaque bandit exploration in production by precomputing a Pareto-dominance lattice per (model, arch, seqlen-bucket). The dominance-tree is built from microbenchmarks per primitive (attention variants, matmul kernels) and recomputed weekly or upon new model rollouts. The replayer is deterministic and models prefix vs decode phase differences explicitly; token-phase bucketing used to improve fidelity. Trade-offs: simulator complexity vs accuracy; we prioritize conservative estimates to minimize rollback frequency.
implementation_plan: 1) Trace normalizer + replayer (week 1): convert request logs -> phase-aware event stream; implement seqlen and token-phase histogram builders. 2) Microbench harness (week 1-2): lightweight per-arch primitive profiling runner; store results in compact CSV. 3) Dominance-tree generator (week 2): build algorithm to compute non-dominated kernel mixes and score vectors. 4) Simulator + calibration (week 3): run end-to-end replay and compare to prod traces; iterate on latency model. 5) Integration PR + canary plan (week 4): expose selector output via /configs endpoint and runtime feature flag. 6) Docs and runbook (week 4).
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff — scoped success metrics and acceptance criteria with PM and infra. Identified data sources: request logs from prod-shard-7 and microbench runner template.
2025-02-18: Prototype replayer implements seqlen bucketing and token-phase tagging; initial reproductions match production seqlen histogram +/- 2.8%.

2025-02-22: Microbench harness completed for CUDA A100 and RTX6000; measured primitives: attention-blockwise, fused-kv, qkv-matmul; stored results in s3://redwood-inference/microbench/eng-53177/latest.csv (internal link).

2025-02-26: First dominance-tree generator produced 18 non-dominated kernel mixes for gpt-3-like model at seqlen=512. Simulator predicted P95 improvements for mix #4 at -12% and cost +3% relative to baseline. Commmented trade-offs in design doc.

2025-03-02: Calibration run against held-out week on prod-shard-3: simulator P50 error 6.5%, P95 error 9.8% (within acceptance). Logged discrepancies tied to KV-cache hit assumptions; added token-phase cache decay parameter in the model.

2025-03-04: Internal design review with Runtime and SRE. Agreed to limit weekly auto-recompute and require manual approval for model rollouts by PM. Opened integration PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1921.
next_steps: Finish PR feedback loop, add KV-cache decay calibration sweep, run full-week replay for top 10 customer workloads, author runbook for safe rollback and canary metrics (tail-latency & error-rate triggers).
